Performers
Musopen Symphony (as credited on Commons) (orchestra) Documented

Commons credits “Musopen Symphony” as the artist. No conductor and no orchestra other than this credit are named in the sources consulted.

[1]
Work version
Orchestral tableau in one continuous movement; edition not identified Inferred, not documented

The Commons description gives only the title. The Musopen listing is for the orchestral piece.

[1] [2]
Recorded
2012 Documented

Commons dates the file 2012; the Musopen Kickstarter project that released the piece to the public domain completed in 2012. Whether 2012 is the session, release or upload date is not stated, so only the year is used.

[1] [2]
Place
Unknown Unknown

No venue or city is given.

[1] [2]
Label
Musopen (Kickstarter-funded recording project) Documented

Musopen is a non-profit that raised money to record music and release it to the public domain.

[1] [2]
Catalogue
Unknown Unknown

The Internet Archive collection has no catalogue number.

[2]
Transfer
Uploaded to Wikimedia Commons by user Kcx36 Documented

Commons file history; the upload comment names the Internet Archive’s Musopen collection as the source. No mastering engineer is named.

[1]
Transfer date
2024-11-12 Documented

Commons upload date, not a session date.

[1]
Processing
FLAC file on Commons; MP3 access derivative generated by Commons Documented

No editing or normalisation by Contrapunctus; one complete source stream. The Internet Archive collection also holds a duplicate of the file.

[1]
Composition rights
Public domain under ordinary life-plus-70 terms Inferred, not documented

Borodin died on 27 February 1887. This says nothing about any modern edition.

[3]
Recording rights
Public domain by Musopen’s release (Creative Commons Public Domain Mark); Commons tags the recording {{PD-author}} for Musopen Documented

The Internet Archive collection of the Musopen Kickstarter recordings carries the Public Domain Mark and lists Borodin’s In the Steppes of Central Asia. Commons quotes Musopen’s requirement that uploaders warrant that content is in the public domain.

[1] [2]

Alexander Borodin, In the Steppes of Central Asia; Musopen Symphony, Musopen Kickstarter Project, 2012. Public domain; via Wikimedia Commons. No audio edits. Rights statement
